giver.resource: the human-rights instruments that ground data sovereignty (privacy of stored/communicated data)

instruments.name: Universal Declaration of Human Rights, Article 12
instruments.right: privacy — no arbitrary interference with privacy, family, home, or correspondence

instruments.name: International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights, Article 17
EU Charter of Fundamental Rights, Article 8
instruments.right: protection of personal data — processed fairly, on consent or a legitimate basis, with access and rectification

instruments.name: Council of Europe Convention 108+ (CETS 223)
instruments.right: the only binding multilateral treaty on automatic processing of personal data

instruments.name: CARE Principles for Indigenous Data Governance (Global Indigenous Data Alliance)
instruments.right: Collective benefit, Authority to control, Responsibility, Ethics

note: A curated index over the named instruments (prose, not parseable data — disclosed as received, not derived, the same way the operator-precedence table is). Data sovereignty has no single UDHR-equivalent declaration; it is fragmented across a treaty, a charter article, a regulation, and an Indigenous framework. This prior assembles the common architectural shapes those instruments license, so a generator can GRAVITATE toward them rather than cite them.

principles.name: end-to-end encryption
principles.note: the data is unreadable to any operator — privacy by construction, not by policy

principles.name: local-first
principles.note: the person's data lives on their device and syncs peer-to-peer; the server is not the home

principles.name: zero-knowledge
principles.note: the operator never holds plaintext or keys

principles.name: data minimization
principles.note: collect and retain the least the task requires

principles.name: deletion and portability
principles.note: the person can delete their data and take it with them

principles.name: self-hosting and open protocol
principles.note: no single operator owns the layer — federation over centralization
